input: Deep condition and trim my natural hair monthly

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Knowing whether this is just deep conditioning and trimming, or a fuller wash day routine (co-wash, protein treatments, styling), determines how much needs to be planned and scheduled.
Whether the trim is done at home or at a salon changes the logistics, cost, and scheduling of the task entirely.
The amount of time available on the chosen day affects whether both the deep condition and trim can realistically happen in one session or need to be split.
Whether they do everything solo or have someone help (e.g., a stylist, friend, or family member) shapes the steps and dependencies in the plan.
Knowing what deep conditioning products they already have vs. need to buy determines whether a shopping or restocking step is needed in the monthly plan.
Hair type, porosity, and length influence which deep conditioner method works best (heat cap, steam, overnight) and how the routine should be sequenced.
Understanding what success looks like — retained length, reduced breakage, moisture balance — helps prioritize which parts of the routine to emphasize and how to track progress.

gold.taskTitle: Deep condition and trim natural hair monthly
gold.taskDescription: Build a consistent monthly routine that includes deep conditioning and trimming natural hair to maintain its health and growth.

questions.title: What else is included beyond deep conditioning and trimming?
questions.description: Does the monthly routine also include steps like co-washing, protein treatments, scalp care, or styling — or is it strictly the two tasks mentioned?

questions.title: Will you trim at home or visit a salon?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan needs to account for booking appointments, travel, and cost, or focus on at-home tools and technique.

questions.title: How many hours can you set aside on hair day?
questions.description: Knowing the available time block helps determine if the deep condition and trim fit into one session or need to be scheduled separately.

questions.title: Do you handle your hair entirely solo?
questions.description: Clarifies whether a stylist, friend, or family member is involved, which affects scheduling dependencies and the steps needed in the plan.

questions.title: Which deep conditioning products do you already own?
questions.description: Identifies whether a product restocking or shopping step needs to be built into the monthly routine before each session.

questions.title: What is your hair type, porosity, and current length?
questions.description: These factors determine the best deep conditioning method (heat cap, steam, overnight soak) and inform how the routine should be structured.

questions.title: What does a successful month of hair care look like to you?
questions.description: Understanding the goal — retained length, less breakage, improved moisture — helps prioritize routine steps and define a way to track progress over time.
